phrases.text: So welcome back again.
It's time to solve one more problem.
Now, in this problem,
two points are on the same side of a balloon.
The distance between these two points is one hundred meter.
From one point,
the angle of elevation is sixty degrees.
From the other point,
the angle of elevation is thirty degrees.
The nearer point has the bigger angle,
that is
sixty degrees,
and we need to find the height of the balloon.
Let the distance from the nearer point to the point exactly below the balloon be x meter.
So the distance from the farther point will be x plus one hundred meter.
Now, we will use the tan formula
because it deals with the base and height.
So
tan theta is equal to height
by base.
From the nearer point,
tan sixty degree is equal to h by x.
Root three is equal to h by x.
So
h is equal to x root three.
Keep this height with us for a second. From the farther point,
tan thirty degree is equal to h by x plus one hundred.
One by root three is equal to h by
x plus one hundred.
So
h is equal to
x plus one hundred
by root three.
Now, both these expressions are for the same height of the same balloon,
so we can make them equal.
X root three is equal to x plus one hundred by root three.
Multiplying both sides by root three,
this becomes
three x is equal to x plus
one hundred.
So two x is equal to one hundred.
Hence,
x is equal to fifty.
Now, we are not asked for x. We are asked for the height of the balloon,
and height h is equal to x root three.
So
h is equal to fifty root three meters.
So the final answer will be option D,
fifty root three meter.
